title: Etale local finite restriction of a closed affine relation
statement: Let $T,U,R$ be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $U\to T$ be locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], and let $s,t:R\to U$ be etale morphisms over $T$ [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Suppose $j=(s,t):R\to U\times_TU$ is a closed immersion [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-closed-immersion] identifying $R(H)$ with an equivalence relation on $U(H)$ for every $T$-scheme $H$. For every $u\in U$, with image $p\in T$, there exist an affine scheme $T'$, an etale map $T'\to T$, a point $p'\in T'$ over $p$ inducing an isomorphism of residue fields [def-weil-residue-field], and decompositions into open and closed subschemes $U\times_TT'=U'\amalg W$, $R\times_TT'=R'\amalg W'$, with a point $u'\in U'$ over both $u$ and $p'$, such that $U'$ and $R'$ are finite over $T'$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and $R'=U'\times_{U\times_TT',s}(R\times_TT')\times_{t,U\times_TT'}U'$ as a restricted relation. The restricted projections $s',t':R'\to U'$ are etale and form an equivalence relation. Open and closed subschemes have their induced scheme structures [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tag 03X5 (lemma-quasi-finite-over-base-j-proper), specialized to an affine etale equivalence relation with closed relation map; conclusions (a), (d), (g), (h), with an affine shrinking of the etale neighbourhood.

proof.text: Write $f:U\to T$ for the structure map. It is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-locally-finite-type], and separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated], since $U$ is affine. Local quasi-finiteness means in particular that $f$ is quasi-finite at the chosen $u$. Therefore $u$ is an isolated point of the scheme-theoretic fibre over $p=f(u)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-point-isolated]. These are exactly the hypotheses needed for the isolated-point splitting theorem.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-splits-off-isolated-points-technical] to $f$, $p$, and the singleton list $(u)$. It gives an elementary etale neighbourhood $(S_1,p_1)\to(T,p)$ and a decomposition $U\times_TS_1=V\amalg W_1$ into open and closed subschemes with $V\to S_1$ finite and a point $v\in V$ over both $u$ and $p_1$. In particular the induced map $\kappa(p)\to\kappa(p_1)$ is an isomorphism. The order of the fibre-product factors is changed using the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product].

Choose an affine open neighbourhood $T'\subseteq S_1$ of $p_1$ and denote the same point by $p'$. Its inclusion is etale, so $T'\to T$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The residue field at a point is unchanged on an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion], hence $\kappa(p)\to\kappa(p')$ is still an isomorphism. Pulling back the decomposition gives $U\times_TT'=U'\amalg W$, where $U'=V\times_{S_1}T'$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a). The point $v$ lies in this inverse image and gives $u'\in U'$ over $u$ and $p'$. The open neighbourhood exists because schemes are locally affine [def-pc-scheme].

source.place: Tag 02LN, restriction to an affine neighbourhood; morphisms.tex Tags 01WL (lemma-base-change-finite), 02GP (lemma-open-immersion-etale), 02GN (lemma-composition-etale)

proof.text: Put $U_0=U\times_TT'$, $R_0=R\times_TT'$, and write $s_0,t_0:R_0\to U_0$ for the pulled-back projections. Define $R'$ to be the induced open subscheme with underlying subset $s_0^{-1}(U')\cap t_0^{-1}(U')$, and let $W'$ be its induced open complement. Both inverse images are open and closed, so their intersection and its complement are open and closed. Thus $R_0=R'\amalg W'$. For every $T'$-scheme $H$, a map $H\to R_0$ factors through $R'$ exactly when its two composites to $U_0$ factor through $U'$, and the factorizations are unique. By [def-pc-fibre-product] this identifies $R'$ with $U'\times_{U_0,s_0}R_0\times_{t_0,U_0}U'$ as schemes, with the stated projections. This also identifies $R'$ with the pullback of $j:R\to U\times_TU$ along $U'\times_{T'}U'\to U\times_TU$.

source.place: Tag 03X5 (lemma-quasi-finite-over-base-j-proper), restriction in (h); direct construction for closed j

proof.text: The map $R'\to U'\times_{T'}U'$ is a closed immersion: its pullback square with $j$ was identified in step 4, so apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. It is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]. The projection $U'\times_{T'}U'\to U'$ is a base change of the finite map $U'\to T'$, hence finite; its composite with $U'\to T'$ is finite. Composing once more with $R'\to U'\times_{T'}U'$ proves $R'\to T'$ finite. The base-change and composition assertions here are precisely the finite-morphism clauses of [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange]; they do not require any radicial hypothesis.

The maps $s_0,t_0:R_0\to U_0$ are base changes of $s,t$, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Since $R'\hookrightarrow R_0$ is an open immersion, the composites $R'\to R_0\rightrightarrows U_0$ are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1),(2). Each factors through the etale open immersion $U'\hookrightarrow U_0$; part (3) of the same node then gives that the factors $s',t':R'\to U'$ are etale.

For a $T'$-scheme $H$, maps $H\to U_0$ over $T'$ identify with maps $H\to U$ over $T$, and similarly for $R_0$, by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus $R_0(H)$ is an equivalence relation on $U_0(H)$ by the hypothesis. The open immersion identifies $U'(H)$ with a subset of $U_0(H)$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Step 4 says exactly that $R'(H)$ is the restriction of that relation to this subset. Reflexivity holds because $(a,a)$ is related for each $a\in U'(H)$; symmetry holds because reversing a related pair still has both entries in the subset; transitivity holds because if $(a,b)$ and $(b,c)$ are related then so is $(a,c)$ and both endpoints remain in the subset. This proves the required equivalence-relation assertion for every $H$, completing all the conclusions.

proof_origin.place: Tag 03X5, specialized argument using Tag 02LN (more-morphisms.tex). split_report.summary: Checked 03X5 and 02LN. Retained the statement. Split off a single finite clopen U-piece by existing 02LN, shrink the base to an affine open, construct the restricted relation as a clopen inverse image, and prove its finiteness by closed immersion into the finite square. Etaleness follows by base change and cancellation against the target open immersion; the equivalence axioms restrict pointwise. No new nodes.

It is a created auxiliary node, not the key Rankin–Selberg unit statement.

tool_uses.why: Generic locality of finite type for the stated locally quasi-finite morphism; no node in this unit states it.
Generic characterization of quasi-finiteness by isolated fibre points, needed to apply 02LN; this unit has no such characterization.
The existing elementary etale finite-piece splitting theorem 02LN is the geometric tool used by the 03X5 route, not a replacement for the unit argument.
Only its general finite-morphism base-change and composition clauses are used to make the restricted relation finite; this unit has no permanence theorem.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N1-29d42e667 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item and its 7 steps, the statement of every cited node, the parent node that uses the item (lem-a1-separated-locally-qf-space-representable), and the unit record. On the source side I read Stacks 03X5 and 03X4 in full (more-groupoids.tex, lemma-quasi-finite-over-base-j-proper and lemma-quasi-finite-over-base) and 02LN (more-morphisms.tex, lemma-etale-splits-off-quasi-finite-part-technical). The statement is unchanged and keeps conclusions (a), (d), (g) and (h) of 03X5 for an affine étale equivalence relation whose relation map j is a closed immersion. It also adds étaleness of s' and t', which step 6 proves. The parent uses exactly these conclusions. Step checks: step 1 gives locally finite type (01TD remark), separatedness (01KN/01KV, since U is affine) and that u is isolated in its fibre (01TH). These are exactly the hypotheses of 02LN with n=1. Step 2 takes from the 02LN node the elementary étale neighbourhood, so κ(p)≅κ(p'). Step 3 shrinks to an affine open and uses only clause (a) of the finite-permanence node. Step 4 is genuinely elementary: R' is the clopen set s0^{-1}(U')∩t0^{-1}(U'), and as a scheme it is the pullback of j. Step 5 shows R'→U'×_{T'}U' is a closed immersion, hence finite (035C), and that the square is finite over T'. It uses only the finite base-change and composition clauses of a Mathlib leaf. Step 6 is étale base change, then composition with an open immersion, then cancellation (02GW). Step 7 restricts the equivalence relation to the subset U'(H). Edge cases tested: U=T=Spec k with the diagonal relation; two points with the total relation, where the chosen piece U' need not be R-invariant and the item does not claim it is; a base point whose residue field is not that of u; U empty. None breaks the statement or the proof. An rg search for 03X5, 03X4 and restricted relations found no duplicate (02WU is a different statement). There are no new nodes and no SGA citation. I accept the declared tool uses: three generic scheme lemmas from sk-thm-p1 and lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange, which is a Mathlib leaf. None of them replaces a step of the unit's route. One cosmetic point: the same verdict text is copied into every search record. I made no fixes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_etale_restricted_relation_neighbourhood {T U R : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T] [IsAffine U] [IsAffine R] (fU : U ⟶ T) (fR : R ⟶ T) (hquasi : Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite fU) (s t : R ⟶ U) (hs : s ≫ fU = fR) (ht : t ≫ fU = fR) (hsEtale : Etale s) (htEtale : Etale t) (j : R ⟶ pullback fU fU) (hj_s : j ≫ pullback.fst fU fU = s) (hj_t : j ≫ pullback.snd fU fU = t) (hj_closed : IsClosedImmersion j) (hrel : ∀ (H : Scheme.{u}) (hH : H ⟶ T), _root_.Equivalence (fun (a b : {g : H ⟶ U // g ≫ fU = hH}) => ∃ r : H ⟶ R, r ≫ s = a.1 ∧ r ≫ t = b.1)) (u : U) : let p : T := fU u ∃ (T' : Scheme.{u}) (f' : T' ⟶ T) (p' : T'), IsAffine T' ∧ Etale f' ∧ f' p' = p ∧ IsIso (f'.residueFieldMap p') ∧ ∃ (Uo Wo : (pullback fU f').Opens), IsCompl Uo Wo ∧ ∃ (u' : Uo.toScheme), pullback.fst fU f' (Uo.ι u') = u ∧ pullback.snd fU f' (Uo.ι u') = p' ∧ IsFinite (Uo.ι ≫ pullback.snd fU f') ∧ ∃ (Ro Wro : (pullback fR f').Opens), IsCompl Ro Wro ∧ IsFinite (Ro.ι ≫ pullback.snd fR f') ∧ let U0 := pullback fU f' let R0 := pullback fR f' let s0 : R0 ⟶ U0 := pullback.map fR f' fU f' s (𝟙 T') (𝟙 T) (by simpa using hs.symm) (by simp) let t0 : R0 ⟶ U0 := pullback.map fR f' fU f' t (𝟙 T') (𝟙 T) (by simpa using ht.symm) (by simp) let P := pullback Uo.ι s0 let Q := pullback (pullback.snd Uo.ι s0 ≫ t0) Uo.ι let p₁ := pullback.fst Uo.ι s0 let p₂ := pullback.snd Uo.ι s0 let q₁ := pullback.fst (pullback.snd Uo.ι s0 ≫ t0) Uo.ι let q₂ := pullback.snd (pullback.snd Uo.ι s0 ≫ t0) Uo.ι ∃ (q : Ro.toScheme ⟶ Q), IsIso q ∧ q ≫ q₁ ≫ p₂ = Ro.ι ∧ Ro.ι ≫ s0 = (q ≫ q₁ ≫ p₁) ≫ Uo.ι ∧ Ro.ι ≫ t0 = (q ≫ q₂) ≫ Uo.ι ∧ Etale (q ≫ q₁ ≫ p₁) ∧ Etale (q ≫ q₂) ∧ ∀ (H : Scheme.{u}) (hH : H ⟶ T'), _root_.Equivalence (fun (a b : {g : H ⟶ Uo.toScheme // g ≫ (Uo.ι ≫ pullback.snd fU f') = hH}) => ∃ r : H ⟶ Ro.toScheme, r ≫ (q ≫ q₁ ≫ p₁) = a.1 ∧ r ≫ (q ≫ q₂) = b.1)
